protocol.lomo: leave-one-out within a fixed three-model training universe (chatgpt/toolllama/gpt-3.5-turbo-1106): a fold holding out one of those three trains on the other two, while the gpt-4-0613 and gpt-4-turbo-preview folds train on all three and are pure cross-model tests. The two gpt-4 families never enter training, so this is NOT a true five-family leave-one-model-out.
protocol.cross_model: train: fixed three-model training set (chatgpt, gpt-3.5-turbo-1106, toolllama); test: gpt-4-0613, gpt-4-turbo-preview
protocol.cross_group: train: G1/G2 queries of the fixed three-model training set; test: independently worded G3_instruction queries (unseen tasks)
protocol.memory_filter: only tool calls inside task-valid trajectories enter success memory
protocol.extractor_learning: per parameter name, pick the best-supported deterministic extractor (ISO dates, month-years, years, quoted keywords, numbers, countries) from successful training calls; unseen parameter names fall back to name-based extractor selection
protocol.schema_funnel: every proposed repair is registered. Tier 1: structural validation checks types, required/extra parameters, enum, format and numeric bounds where the schema declares them; proposed values are first converted to the declared scalar types (schema_type_coercion, counted separately). Tier 2: a schema-invalid proposal is admitted only when it is an exact recorded successful invocation of the same task/function (recorded_success_match). schema_valid_rate = schema_passed / proposed; accepted coverage = (schema_passed + value_verified) / evaluable_failures.
repair_strategies: deterministic schema rules (function-name resolution, drop/rename args, schema defaults, type coercion)
schema default completion when the error names no parameters (unverified proposal)

verification.schema_validity: structural JSON-Schema validation of the agent-visible schema
verification.value_agreement: repaired parameter values equal a recorded successful invocation of the same task/function
verification.cache_verification: repaired call replayed against the released real-response cache (subset only)

results.skipped_no_schema_explanation: A failure-call can only be repaired/evaluated when the failed call has a tool schema (the agent-visible api_list) and parseable arguments. 30 failures carry unparseable raw arguments and 34 target a tool that is absent from the schema index; these 64 failures are counted in dataset.real_failures but excluded from the repair denominator (results.lomo_aggregate.evaluable_failures).

lomo_sensitivity_exclude_fold.note: Sensitivity check: true leave-one-model-out training (every call outside the held-out fold enters training). Not the main protocol; the committed main LOMO numbers keep the historical fixed three-model training set.

key_findings: Offline replay over 30120 evaluated calls from 7636 parsed trajectories: 1033 recorded failures, of which 969 target an indexed tool with parseable arguments (64 skipped_no_schema: 30 raw arguments, 34 tool not in schemas).

Evidence funnel (LOMO): 583 proposed repairs; 472 pass the declared structural schema (81.0%; 150 of them after deterministic type coercion), 111 proposals are schema-rejected for their failure; 59 schema-invalid proposals are admitted only because they are exact recorded successful invocations of the same task/function. Accepted repairs = 472 + 59 = 531/969 (54.8% coverage).

Cross-task generalisation (cross_group): 57/76 evaluable failures repaired (75.0%); decomposition: 30 schema-valid (type-coerced schema defaults) + 27 value-verified learned text-extraction repairs (the upstream api_list declares those date parameters as number, while both the extractor and the recorded successful calls use ISO date strings).

Learned text-extractor repairs: cross_model 12 accepted (all value-verified), cross_group 27 accepted (all value-verified, value agreement 27/27); value agreement with a recorded successful call is reported per category and is a strict lower bound on verified repairs.
Cache verification found 0 regressions: every verified cache replay returned a recorded successful response, while cache misses stay unverified (not failures).

LOMO protocol: leave-one-out inside the fixed three-model training universe (chatgpt, gpt-3.5-turbo-1106, toolllama); the gpt-4 families are test-only, so these numbers are NOT a true five-family leave-one-model-out. The true-LOMO sensitivity run is reported separately.
limitations: Offline replay only: no live API/tool execution in this artifact.

Two evidence tiers are reported, never mixed into one rate: (1) schema-valid (full structural JSON-Schema validation of the declared schema: type/required/extra/enum/format/range, with deterministic type coercion attempted first and counted in coerced_repairs); (2) value-verified (schema-invalid proposals admitted only when they are an exact recorded successful invocation of the same task/function). schema_valid_rate = schema_passed / proposed; it is NOT 100% by construction.

The declared agent-visible schema itself has fidelity limits: the upstream StableToolBench api_list declares some date parameters as number (while recorded successful calls use ISO date strings) and leaves some function parameter lists empty. These are the cases where the value-verified tier is needed; they are reported, not silently relaxed.
64 failures are excluded as skipped_no_schema (see results.skipped_no_schema_explanation); they remain in dataset.real_failures.
The released response cache covers reference-solution inputs only; repaired calls that miss the cache cannot be verified (cache_miss in each protocol); cache misses are not failures.
Value agreement is only checkable when some model solved the same task instance; it is a strict lower bound on verified repairs.
Schema-default completion is a proposal, not verified evidence; unverified proposals are reported separately and are not counted as quality evidence.
Server-side/transient errors are not repaired deterministically offline.
The LOMO label follows the historical fixed three-model training set; the true leave-one-model-out sensitivity numbers are included under results.lomo_sensitivity_exclude_fold.
The parser treats unparseable observation payloads as successful responses (dataset.unparseable_observations_treated_as_success counts them); such calls can hide a failure.
Single repair direction: the middleware does not modify tool implementations or agent prompts in this artifact.
